name: Père Fouettard
description: St Nicholas's grim, black-robed servant, who carries the whip so the saint doesn't have to
origin: Folklore of north-east France and Wallonia in Belgium

debut.title: French and Walloon St Nicholas tradition
debut.era: medieval legend, still walking in parades today

legend: On 6 December, St Nicholas parades through towns in Lorraine and Wallonia handing out gifts, and a step behind him walks Père Fouettard, Father Whipper, in dark robes with a wild beard and a bundle of switches. The best-known story of his origin is a grim one: a butcher lured three boys into his shop, killed them and salted them away in a barrel. St Nicholas found them and brought them back to life, and the repentant butcher was bound to follow the saint ever after, punishing the children who don't deserve presents.

myths.explanation: Fouet is French for whip, and the switch or whip is his trademark.

myths.claim: Père Fouettard comes on Christmas Day.
myths.explanation: He walks with St Nicholas on 6 December, St Nicholas Day.

myths.claim: His legend involves St Nicholas raising three children from the dead.
myths.explanation: In the best-known version, the saint revives three boys killed by a butcher, who becomes his penitent servant.

powers: A whip or bundle of switches
A list of every naughty child
weaknesses: Children with nothing to answer for
legacy: St Nicholas parades in Nancy and other towns of Lorraine every December
Hans Muff, his German-speaking cousin in the Rhineland
